div.head: Had 10
div.ab: Áá sceal mid rihte dóm æfter dǽde ⁊ medemung be mæðe for Gode ⁊ for worlde.
Á sceal mid rihte dóm æfter dæde ⁊ myltsung be mæðe for Gode ⁊ for worulde.
A man sceal mid rihte dom æfter dæde ⁊ medemung be mæþe for Gode ⁊ for worulde.
[10] Semper enim debet iudicium . . . factum et moderatio secundum mensuram pro Deo et seculo fieri.
A man sceal mid rihte dom æfter dæde and medemung be mæþe for Gode and for worulde.
Immer gehört sich von rechtswegen das Urtheil gemäss der Missethat und [Straf]abmessung (Milderung O) nach dem Range [des Verletzten] in Kirchlichem und in Weltlichem.
Always, by right, judgment belongs according to the misdeed, and the measuring [of punishment] (mitigation, O) according to the rank [of the injured man], in matters of God and of the world.
There must always by rights be sentence according to the deed, and apportioning [of the penalty] according to the degree, in ecclesiastical and secular concerns.
One must always pass a judgment appropriate for the deed and set a penalty appropriate for the rank in both divine and secular affairs.
div.note: In H, 10 stands before 9.1 (as in hq). K: a stray ‘7’ removed (H begins ‘A man’). Supply ‘secundum’ in the Quadripartitus gap. Liebermann compares VIII Atr 5.2.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘There must always by rights be sentence according to the degree, in ecclesiastical and secular concerns.’).
